As Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Manager, the staged cooling load fits the insulated box with margin for control, Enclosure and Structural Designer.

In plain words thick foam holds steady leak well below harvest heat so the cooler holds temperature not just pulls down. Transmission is 203 watt in the conduction estimate (E41) inside 615 watt staged average in the revised steady-load simulation (E28), with daily 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day in the steady plus staged pull-down estimate (E58), about one household daily use in everyday scale, so 100 millimetre walls with 120 millimetre roof and floor at heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin from Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) is the insulation requirement.

As Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, I confirm your door choice keeps door heat to kettles, Enclosure and Structural Designer.

In plain words one narrow door with curtain opened by day lets little warm air in. I take up the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) you put on the board, which states 900 millimetre doors with Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC, flexible plastic) strip curtains and self-closing hinges, which from refrigeration means 4 air changes per day cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, by the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51), so 8 openings discipline holds.

As Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, serviceability keeps non-flammable refrigerant with small efficiency cost while shade helps the condenser, Enclosure and Structural Designer.

In plain words village repair favours seals and gauges over peak lab efficiency. R134a (tetrafluoroethane, A1 non-flammable refrigerant) stays field-serviceable per R134a vs R290 Refrigerant: Key Differences & Replacements (E17) against the hot-climate penalty in A solar powered off-grid air conditioning system with natural refrigerant (E23), with Coefficient of Performance (COP, cooling per electric power) about 1.4 at hot ambient, and I take up the PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels | Commercial & High-Performance (E64) you put on the board for the 2-module roof sunshade vent gap, which from refrigeration cuts roof plus shaded-condenser lift in hot-dry peaks. I am ready on version one, because load, box, door and refrigerant close with only the 43 degree pull-down bench test left as named hardware test.
